text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- The opposition blocked the approval of a draft law on customs tariffs by frequently calling for recesses.
- The state court reversed the guilty sentence of Tallinn district court on lawyer Monika Magi, accused of offering a bribe to a judge.
- Estonian and U.S. representatives signed the agreement on the military exercise Baltic Challenge, which will be held in and around Paldiski in July.
- The government refused to admit a Chechen parliamentary delegation to Estonia, claiming that Estonia does not recognise their Soviet internal passports.
SONUMILEHT
- The Fatherland Union and the right-wing opposition announced that they prefer domestic peace and cooperation in the government and opposition in order to achieve EU entry.

- Academician Ando Raukas will leave the Coalition Party in protest against Justice Minister's Paul Varul's interpretation of the law on the basics of ownership reform. The minister Paul has illegally refused to return the property of thousands of people, Raukas said.
- Denmark donated a mobile radiation detection and measuring lab to the radiation protection centre.
EESTI PAEVALEHT
- The Tallinn plant of Finnish electronics concern Elcoteq will produce Ericsson miniature mobile phones GF 788. Full production volume will be achieved by the end of the year.
- An opinion poll published shows that the people do not know their parliament deputies and consider the influence of the financial circles on legislation excessive.
- The president appointed 10 new judges.
POSTIMEES
- The Russian Embassy announced that deported ex-Soviet officer Yevgeni Zobnin has been retired since 1993. He was refused a residence permit as being a reserve officer.

- The magazine LUUP claims that its accusations on the defence ministry losing money on fuel contracts can be confirmed. Defence Minister Andrus Oovel has threatened the magazine with a lawsuit for slander.
ARIPAEV
- A publishing and printing firm plan to open Estonia's first and largest book department store in Tartu
